observations: Nikon DSLR camera body with a body cap attached.
The model badge 'D610' is clearly visible on the front right of the camera.
The 'FX' badge indicating a full-frame sensor is visible.
The camera has a neck strap attached.
The rear LCD screen is shown turned off.
There is visible wear and scuffing on the bottom corners and edges of the body in photo 1.
No lens is included in the photos.
Watermark 'POSTED ON JIJI CHIMEZIE HILLS' appears on all photos.

claims.evidence: Photo 0 and 2 clearly show the model badge as 'D610'.
Photo 1 shows scuffing and wear on the bottom edges of the camera body.

risks.risk: Sensor may be scratched, dusty, or have fungus.
risks.proof: A clear, close-up photo of the sensor with the body cap removed.
risks.if_unproven: as a damaged sensor requiring replacement

risks.risk: The shutter may be near its end of life (high shutter count).
risks.proof: A screenshot of the shutter count from a tool like 'CameraShutterCount' using the last photo taken.
risks.if_unproven: as having a very high shutter count near failure

risks.risk: The camera may not power on or the LCD may be broken.
risks.proof: A photo or video of the camera powered on with the LCD displaying a menu or image.

risks.risk: Battery and charger may be missing.
risks.proof: A photo showing the battery and the specific Nikon charger.
risks.if_unproven: as missing both battery and charger

proof_requests: Photo of the camera powered on showing the LCD screen working.
Photo of the sensor with the body cap removed.
The current shutter count of the camera.
Photos of the battery and charger.
response.reason: The item is clearly identified as a Nikon D610 despite the seller's typo. It can be priced at its worst-case value (non-functional, body only) until further proof is provided.
